citations.quote: When standard arithmetic is in effect, the result of the initial evaluation is equivalent to the result of the arithmetic expression
When standard-decimal arithmetic or standard-binary arithmetic is in effect, the result of the initial evaluation is equivalent
The result shall be the exact sum truncated to 32 significant digits
A standard intermediate data item shall be rounded to 31 digits in the situations listed below

cases.reason: The differing words are the arithmetic mode: 2002 names 'standard arithmetic' (the 32-digit decimal floating-point standard intermediate data item of 8.8.1.3), 2023 names standard-decimal/standard-binary. The pointer's evidence for the standard arm is STANDARD-DECIMAL (34-digit), refused at 2002. Probe p01-add-std (ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD, --std 2002): ADD A B C E TO F GIVING R with A=B=10**31-1, C=.01, E=F=-(10**31-1): (A+B)+C has 34 digits, cut to 32 the .01 is lost, so R must be +0.00; the compiler prints +0.01. ADD H TO N GIVING R2 (N=10**30, H=.5): 32 digits, rounded to 31 at the transfer gives 10**30+1; the compiler prints 10**30. This is kb/Work PB5575 (known, open; its run-time arm landed on main after the pinned build, not verified here); not a new defect.
cases.needs: its own verdict: at --std 2002 (pinned build) ADD format 2 under ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD keeps 34 digits (p01: F2-TRUNC R=+0.01, expected +0.00; F2-ROUND R2=10**30, expected 10**30+1) = PB5575; re-probe p01 on a build carrying PB5575's run-time arm and use it as the 2002 witness

cases.reason: The reader's 'specified' = 'specified or implied' reading holds (2002 14.1.3 GR4 and CALL GR9 a) make a literal reading absurd). But SR16 governs every argument of the program-prototype format, and 2002 SR3 (ALL FORMATS, so format 3 too) admits identifier-2 from the communication section, which 2023 SR3 excludes. A record item under a CD passed BY REFERENCE / BY CONTENT to a prototype call is in the 2002 scope of SR16 and in no 2023 program, so the 2023 row's tests (all working-storage arguments) do not show it. Probes at --std 2002: r1 (CD item BY REFERENCE to a BY VALUE formal) and r2 (BY CONTENT) are refused with COBOL1687; r3 (legal pairs, explicit and keyword-less, assumed BY REFERENCE formal) runs: CR1=AAAA CR2=YYYY / CR1=XXXX CR2=YYYY. Compiler-at-2002: correct for the CD case; r1/r2/r3 are the candidate 2002 witnesses. Second reach (same defect the reader filed under GR7): 2002 has no same-signature rule for CALL restricted-pointer AS prototype (2023 SR14 is new), so SR16 also governs that 2002-only call, which the compiler refuses at 2002 with COBOL2936 (r8).

cases.reason: The rule text and its referenced omitted-argument condition (2002 8.8.4.1.7 = 2023 8.8.4.8) are the same. But GR11 governs every 2002 format-3 CALL, and 2002 permits a CALL through a restricted program-pointer naming a prototype with a different signature: 2002 GR7 lets either prototype determine the characteristics and 2002 has no same-signature CALL rule (2002 USAGE GR17 restricts only the pointer's content); 2023 added SR14, which forbids that call. So GR11's 2002 scope includes calls 2023 has no program for, and the 2023 row says nothing about them. Probe r8: PA restricted to PRA (USING OPTIONAL L-N), CALL PA AS PRB USING OMITTED with PRB = USING OPTIONAL L-N OPTIONAL L-M (OMITTED and the trailing omission are legal under either prototype): 2002 requires 'L-N OMITTED' in PRA; the compiler refuses at --std 2002 with COBOL2936 citing §2023:14.9.4.3 SR14.
